[JISHUMI:v10p7162/r22] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The keepers' number is a trial and test for disbelievers, who are challenged to believe it, and a test for the People of the Book concerning the Prophet's truthfulness.
[JISHUMI:v10p7162/r23] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الأصم | reports | Al-Aṣamm says the small number is a test to show that God can strengthen them so that they can do the work of a much larger number.
[JISHUMI:v10p7162/r24] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | The People of the Book, Jews and Christians, are to become certain the report is true because it agrees with their scriptures.
[JISHUMI:v10p7162/r25] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | Another view says the number proves that God can give one being strength equal to that of many.

[JISHUMI:v10p7162/r27] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | One explanation is that believers' faith is first made manifest, then grows stronger.
[JISHUMI:v10p7162/r28] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | Another explanation says believers grow in faith because the report conveys what only God could know, so they recognize it as a miracle and God's speech.

[JISHUMI:v10p7162/r30] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | One explanation takes the lām as the lām of consequence: they hear it and say this while intending disbelief; another takes it as a prediction of what they will say.
[JISHUMI:v10p7162/r31] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | prefers | Although one view takes those with sickness in their hearts as hypocrites, the author favors dissent and disbelief because the verse is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy there.
[JISHUMI:v10p7162/r32] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | One view says the disbelievers ask what the count nineteen means and grow more doubtful.

[JISHUMI:v10p7162/r36] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | Another explanation says God rules that people are astray or guided according to what He finds in them.
[JISHUMI:v10p7162/r37] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | As He consigns this disbeliever to Saqar, God likewise deals with whom He wills by leading astray or rewarding them.

[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The guardians of Hell are angels, not humans, so no one can overpower them; their number nineteen tests and misleads unbelievers.

[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r6] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | وما هي refers to Saqar, which serves as a reminder and admonition to humanity.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | reports | An unnamed preceding boast says the least among them would enter the Fire and then they would pass into Paradise; the verse was revealed in response.

[KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r3] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | It is called Umm al-Qurʾān because it contains the Qurʾān’s meanings: praise of God, worship through commands and prohibitions, and promise and threat.

[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r13] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Calling the number a parable borrows from unusual speech and conveys astonishment that God chose nineteen rather than twenty, implying a defective number and nondivine origin.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r14] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The كاف is accusative, and كذلك points back to the account of guidance and misguidance.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r15] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Believers see God's wise act as wisdom and gain faith; disbelievers deny or doubt it and increase in disbelief and error.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r16] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Only God knows each host's exact number and its wisdom, as with the counts of creation, calendar divisions, stars, and prescribed acts.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r17] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | reports | Alternatively, only God knows the armies because they are innumerable; nineteen does not limit His power, and the number has hidden wisdom.

[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r2] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | reports | Abū Jahl mocked the nineteen and challenged Quraysh to overpower them; Abū al-Ashadd volunteered to handle seventeen, and the revelation answered that the guardians are angels, not vulnerable men.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r3] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | reports | Abū al-Ashadd ibn Usayd ibn Kalda, described as strong, offered to handle seventeen guardians and asked the others to handle two.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r4] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The reply says guardians are angels rather than men of the disbelievers' kind who can be overpowered.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r5] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The trial itself is not the cause of the outcomes; the number nineteen is substituted with a number liable to cause that trial.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r6] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | People of Scripture recognize nineteen from their books and take it as confirmation of the Qur'an's divine origin, while unbelievers mock the number.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r7] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Believers grow in faith by accepting this as they accepted other revelations and by seeing Scripture readers confirm it.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r8] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Stating certainty and absence of doubt emphasizes believers' composure and contrasts them with doubting hypocrites and unbelievers.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r9] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Although hypocrisy arose in Medina, this Meccan verse predicts the hypocrites who would appear there after the Hijra.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Only angels guard Hell, refuting Quraysh: their number tests unbelievers by prompting presumptuous talk and ambition.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهم | reports | People of the Book recognize the Quran as from God because the number matches their revealed books, which Muhammad neither read nor belonged to their community; the scriptures confirm one another.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Revelation of truths from God increases believers' faith and removes doubt from believing People of the Book and the faithful.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Those with sickness of heart are a hypocritical or unbelieving group who go astray and question the example contemptuously.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الحسين بن الفضل | reports | Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl says the sura is Meccan and had no hypocrisy in Mecca, so sickness here means agitation and weakness of faith.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | God misguides those whose hearts are rusted and guides believers who know His power and affirm the truth of prophetic revelation and scripture.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Only God knows His forces; the statement indicates that reality exceeds imagination and this is only one part of divine power, since the heavens teem with constantly obedient angels.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says وما هي refers to Hell, whose reminder makes people fear and obey God.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · بعض الحذاق | reports | Some discerning interpreters take وما هي to mean the situation, address, and warning.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الثعلبي | reports | Al-Thaʿlabi reports a view that وما هي means the worldly fire, a reminder of the fire of the afterlife.
[TABRISI:74:25-31/r15] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك | reports | They report that Abu Jahl mocked the nineteen keepers, and Abū al-Asad al-Jumaḥī boasted he could handle seventeen while Quraysh dealt with two; the verse followed.
[TABRISI:74:25-31/r16] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The keepers entrusted with Hell's administration are angels, whose drive is to punish its inhabitants, rather than humans whom people might imagine they could overpower.
[TABRISI:74:25-31/r17] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The number tests and burdens disbelievers, who should reflect that God is wise and could strengthen even one angel to punish all creatures.
[TABRISI:74:25-31/r18] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | A further proof of God's power is that a single angel can be assigned to take the souls of all humanity, so nineteen can drive some people to Hell.
[TABRISI:74:31/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Jews and Christians can confirm the report and Muḥammad's truthfulness because it matches their scriptures, though he neither read them nor learned from them.
[TABRISI:74:31/r10] TABRISI, d. 548 · عطاء | reports | ʿAṭāʾ says only God knows the number of angels made to torment Hell's inhabitants; the nineteen keepers have further forces known only to Him.
[TABRISI:74:31/r11] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Saqar is a reminder and admonition for people to avoid what would merit it.
[TABRISI:74:31/r12] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | Alternatively, the earthly fire is a reminder of the afterlife's fire, prompting people to beware it.
[TABRISI:74:31/r13] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | Another view takes the reminder to be this sūra itself.
[TABRISI:74:31/r14] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | Another view says the nineteen angels are a lesson in God's complete power and a warning against sins.
[TABRISI:74:31/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Believers grow in faith in the number and in Muḥammad's prophethood when the People of the Book confirm it.
[TABRISI:74:31/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The purpose is that both believers and those not yet believing in Muḥammad become certain of his prophethood and do not doubt the keepers' number through reflection.
[TABRISI:74:31/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The lām marks an eventual outcome: hypocrites and unbelievers end up asking what God intended by this description and number.
[TABRISI:74:31/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | Alternatively, the lām expresses purpose: they ask what it means, reflect, and their reflection leads them to faith.
[TABRISI:74:31/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | As with the angels and their number, the test brings error or guidance to light; God is named as its source because the testing obligation comes from Him.
[TABRISI:74:31/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | Alternatively, God misleads whom He wills away from the path to Paradise and reward, and guides whom He wills to it.
[TABRISI:74:31/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Only God knows the innumerable forces He commands; the nineteen were selected by wisdom, not because His forces are few.
[TABRISI:74:31/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · مقاتل | reports | Miqātil says this answers Abū Jahl's taunt that Muḥammad had only nineteen helpers.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · بعض المفسرين | reports | One Qur'anic sense is angels generally; another reported view restricts the phrase to the keepers of Hell.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r10] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · بعض المفسرين | reports | Ashab means the keepers of Hell in 74:31.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The keepers of the Fire are angels, not humans, so who could withstand or overpower them?
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r10] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | As God misguides those who reject the number of keepers, He guides those who believe it.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r11] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The armies are angels God created to punish the people of the Fire; each of the nineteen has helpers whose number only God knows.

[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r13] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الماوردي | reports | Al-Māwardī offers as a possible wisdom that nineteen combines the largest single-digit number, nine, with the smallest number above the single digits, ten.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r14] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The Fire in this world is only a reminder of the Fire of the Hereafter.

[RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | An unattributed report says that after the nineteen keepers were mentioned, Abū Jahl mocked the claim and challenged Quraysh to overpower them; Abū al-Ashadd boasted he could take seventeen while the rest handled two. | mentions 74:30
[RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | The Muslims answered that angels cannot be compared with blacksmiths; the saying became a proverb for two incomparable things, and Rāzī explains the comparison as angels versus jailers and smiths, with the jailer confining the Fire.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Angels were appointed rather than the punished creatures’ own kind because shared kind may incline toward pity; likewise the human messenger is of our kind so he may show compassion.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Angels are furthest from disobeying God and strongest in carrying out arduous acts of obedience.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Their strength exceeds that of jinn and humans.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A hypothetical objection asks how beings created from light could endure staying in fire.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Rāzī replies that God can sustain life indefinitely in severe torment without death, so it is likewise possible for angels to remain in fire without pain.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r8] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The first reason the count tests unbelievers is their mockery: why were the keepers not twenty, and what singled out this number?
[RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r9] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The second objection is that so few keepers seem unable to punish all jinn and humans from creation to the Resurrection; believers do not heed these doubts.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · القائلون بأن الله قد يريد الإضلال | reports | Those who argue that God may will misguidance cite the verse’s statement that the keepers’ number was made a trial for unbelievers.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الجبائي | reports | Al-Jubbāʾī says fitna means making the religious obligation more demanding, so people infer God can empower nineteen to do what one hundred thousand strong angels could not.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الكعبي | reports | Al-Kaʿbī says fitna means a test in which believers entrust the wisdom of the chosen number to the Creator’s knowledge; it is an ambiguous matter they are commanded to accept in faith.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | reports | A third Muʿtazilī answer takes the trial as the disbelief caused when people reject the keepers’ number and make their derisive remarks; this is punishment through withholding divine لطف.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Rāzī replies that the key question is whether ambiguous revelation strengthens the motive to disbelieve: if not, calling it a trial is pointless; if so, the motive to abstain is overcome and disbelief becomes unavoidable.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Rāzī lists four effects of the ambiguous passage: People of Scripture become certain, believers increase in faith, both groups remain free of doubt, and diseased hearts and unbelievers ask what God intended by it.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | For the question why the number is not different, Rāzī notes that every finite world and every bounded body has a definite count; one can equally ask why the world was created at one moment rather than just before or after, or why any created thing has its particular time and parts. No answer is needed beyond God’s free choice among equals, which also explains the nineteen keepers.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The objection from the keepers’ small number is weak: God can grant them strength enough to punish all creatures without failing.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Both objections challenge divine omnipotence; once God’s unlimited power and the afterlife’s unlike worldly conditions are accepted, these improbabilities disappear.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | One construction supplies an omitted coordination: the number is a trial for unbelievers and also serves to make the People of Scripture certain; an “and” may be stated or omitted in such phrasing.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Another construction says “we made their number only nineteen,” using “trial for unbelievers” in place of “nineteen”: the effect is named for its cause because that effect necessarily follows.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | First, this count was already in the People of Scripture’s book; Muḥammad reported the same number without prior study, showing that it came by revelation, which strengthens believers from among them.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Second, although Torah and Gospel readers knew the number, suspected textual alteration made them hesitant to rely on it; hearing it from the Messenger strengthened their faith and certainty in its truth.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Third, Muḥammad knew Quraysh would mock this astonishing detail, as they mocked clearer doctrines; risking ridicule to proclaim it shows his aim was conveying revelation rather than worldly status or pleasing either believers or deniers.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | On Rāzī’s own theological position, there is no difficulty in God intending the unbelievers’ and hypocrites’ response, since God guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | reports | The Muʿtazila say the lām describes an outcome that occurred as though it were an intended purpose, as in 28:8. | mentions 28:8
[RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | They called it a “parable” because the extraordinary number made them suspect that its apparent sense was not intended and that it symbolized another purpose.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Although those with diseased hearts—hypocrites—outwardly acknowledged the Qur’an came from God, they voiced the question as a claim about God’s intent.

[ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Thus, the statement that it is created can refer to the externally uttered image, so proofs of createdness concern that image rather than inward speech and the objection falls away.

[ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · عفيف الدين الإيجي | reports | Al-Iji analyzes a statement into its wording, intended sense, the speaker's knowledge of the relation, and the relation's actual truth; the last two are not speech by consensus, and Ashʿarīs exclude the wording, leaving its meaning.
